A1.justification: Despite the changed title and substantial revision, both PDFs describe UNREAL and retain matching algorithms, experiments and results. Both documents, including their appendices, are sufficiently complete and readable for comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original node-classification experiments, pseudo-label analyses and ablations in Section 5 and Appendices A–C.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds geometric-imbalance analyses, additional benchmark evaluations and runtime measurements, particularly in Appendices E, F and I.

M1.justification: The practical UNREAL procedure retains clustering/classifier agreement, RBO-weighted ranking, the (beta−delta)/delta filtering index and iterative retraining. Renaming DGIN to DGIS and adding a vMF-based theoretical model do not establish a changed algorithm; the corresponding pseudocodes implement the same core steps.

E1.justification: Alongside the retained coverage, v2 evaluates CS-Random/Coauthor-CS, ogbn-arxiv, ogbn-products, Chameleon, Squirrel and Wisconsin. Appendix I also adds CIFAR100LT image classification, substantially extending coverage to larger graphs, heterophilous settings and a non-graph task.

E2.justification: GraphSR and BIM are added to the retained benchmark comparisons. Appendix I additionally evaluates SCR and ConsisGAD, and compares against Co-Training and M3S. The latter two were discussed but not evaluated against UNREAL in v1.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce balanced pretraining and frozen/trainable GNN–MLP controls, reduced training rounds, runtime protocols, and ACC/AUC-ROC evaluation on ogbn-products. The reported GNN depth search expands from 1–3 to 1–4 layers and the clustering search grid changes. Ablation component flags are also reversed, without establishing that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled embedding visualizations, geometric-imbalance/entropy analyses across 50 imbalance scenarios, reduced-round ablations and heterophily robustness tests. Much earlier DPAM, ranking and sensitivity analysis is retained or relocated. The five-region pseudo-label accuracy case study in v1 Appendix C.5/Figure 10 is removed.

E5.justification: Retained benchmark tables still report standard errors over five repetitions. The new ogbn-products experiment explicitly reports standard deviations over five different random seeds. The new checklist also describes error bars as standard deviations, conflicting with the retained standard-error captions; no increase in repeated-run counts is established.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive benchmark, comparator, geometric-analysis and efficiency results while retaining most earlier benchmark scores. It also revises reported values: UNREAL’s Flickr–SAGE balanced accuracy/F1 changes from 50.68/51.01 in v1 Table 6 to 30.68/31.01 in v2 Tables 6 and 26.

T1.justification: v2 introduces hyperspherical vMF modeling, a formal epsilon-geometric-imbalance definition, entropy and class-imbalance theorems, and a ranking-dominance theorem, with proofs in Appendices C, D and H. Appendix I.6 adds computational-complexity analysis. These substantially extend v1’s mathematical definitions and algorithm equations.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from systematically studying self-training and proposing UNREAL’s selection techniques to claiming a rigorous manifold-based characterization of geometric imbalance and its relationships with uncertainty and class imbalance. The abstract and introduction make this theoretical contribution central, while retaining the practical performance claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations connecting message passing to minority-embedding distortion and uncertainty, contrasts GNNs with MLPs, and explicitly distinguishes geometric from topology imbalance. It also explains the practical filtering index as a surrogate for the new theoretical score and discusses K-Means versus manifold-aware clustering tradeoffs.

D1.justification: v2 adds code/project access links, measured training and selection times, additional dataset label statistics, and tuning details for new comparisons and settings. Most optimizer, training, hardware and existing-baseline implementation information is retained from v1 Appendix D in v2 Appendix K.

R1.justification: Section 6 and Appendix B substantially expand discussion of recent self-training, soft pseudo-labeling, topology-bias and hyperspherical modeling research. GraphSR, BIM and IceBerg change the positioning from an early self-training contribution toward a claimed principled explanation and treatment of geometric imbalance.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and substantial portions of the method and experimental narrative are rewritten. New theory precedes the method, earlier self-training motivation moves into Appendix J, and the appendices are extensively reorganized with a contents section and checklist.

P2.justification: v2 changes the main text from two columns to one, redraws the pipeline, adds geometric-imbalance diagrams and diagnostic plots, and restructures benchmark tables into main-text subsets and full appendix versions. Earlier plots are regrouped, and Tables 1/32 reverse the component checkmarks shown in v1 Table 11.

improvement.justification: Broader comparisons, new evaluation domains and runtime information strengthen empirical assessment beyond v1. However, v2 makes new theory central while Appendix C’s entropy bounds conflict for sufficiently small within-class dispersion. Tables 1/32 also invert v1 Table 11’s component flags while retaining almost all scores, undermining ablation interpretation. These substantial evidence additions and new reliability problems prevent a confident judgment of net overall improvement.
